speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if you have experienced any headaches, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light along with your fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of taking haloperidol and the presence of fever with altered mentation, are you experiencing any muscle rigidity, tremors, or excessive sweating? I also need to know if you have had any recent changes in your medication dosage.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have classic signs of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, including fever, rigidity, altered mentation, and diaphoresis while on haloperidol. REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase_LEVEL.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The markedly elevated creatine kinase level of 5600 U/L confirms significant muscle breakdown, which, combined with your fever, rigidity, and altered mental status while on haloperidol, is diagnostic for Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
